Unavailable.description: What the page could not read and why the host said so.

source.description: The artifact the operation went for, named as the site names it.

SpatialCorpusEntry.description: One entry of the committed spatial corpus, as a store runs it: the documents to insert, the query to execute over them, and what the JavaScript engine recorded — a value, or the empty sequence, which JSON cannot spell and null must not stand in for.

dir.description: Repo-relative workspace directory — the base every README URL is built from.

SiteCard.description: A package's card on the site, in the package's own words. `perf` is authored voice — the measured line comes from the benchmark headline its engine names, never from here — so it carries no figure.

SiteEngine.description: One engine card a package contributes to the engine grid: the id the grid and the playground know it by, the benchmark suite whose headline measures it, and the card to render. The card is the engine's own where its document wrote one and the package's card otherwise, resolved by the collector so a reader never has to fall anything back.

ContentEntry.description: One published workspace's site presence. `derived` says where the card came from: false for a workspace that committed its own site document, true for one still described by its manifest alone.

engines.description: The engine cards this workspace contributes, in the order it wants them. Empty for a package that is not an engine — several packages publish more than one, which is why this is a list and not a member.

CardsEntry.description: One published workspace's site presence WITHOUT its documentation body: the same entry site.content carries, minus docs. Nothing derives it independently — the collector projects it from the content entry, so the two can only ever disagree by a member this document does not declare.

RunStamp.description: The invocation that last ran the generator: the machine, the runtime, the suite version and the iteration mode. It describes the RUN, never the rows — those carry their own.

Headline.description: One suite's overview row. The four provenance members are nullable because a row carried from an older file knows only its date, and an unknown is a smaller claim than a plausible lie.

ratio.description: Jaren over the fastest rival; below 1 is a published loss. Null where the suite scores no ratio.

Conformance.description: The scores the overview and the docs page publish. Every block is nullable: a suite the run skipped and no committed file answers for scores nothing, and says so.

engineStats.description: engine → draft → the tests that engine passed, failed and errored on. Each engine is scored over the tests IT ran.

Qt3.description: The XQuery scorecard, parsed from the runner's print format — null when the suite did not run, and a member is null when the line it comes from was not printed.

SuiteCharts.description: charts.json — the chart-type render table, the static line sampling rows (source vs rendered counts, AST and svg), and the two scaling series (points/series, then bar categories) behind the incremental-render claim.

SuiteContract.description: contract.json — the contract dispatch suite: the per-stage pipeline tables and the serialization share of a dispatch.

SuiteContracts.description: contracts.json — the validation front door measured against Zod, as tables of named rows.

SuiteCsv.description: csv.json — the reader and writer against the CSV field, its damage-healing spectrum, and the streaming profile.

SuiteDb.description: db.json — the phase-A store and LINQ front door: one meta block of corpus sizes and equivalence, and the timing tables.

SuiteFlow.description: flow.json — the FSM and DAG engines against XState: compile and transition by machine size, the JSON-survivability wedge, and the memory series.

SuiteFormats.description: formats.json — the format registry against ajv-formats over the formats both engines implement, with the agreement count that gates the timing.

SuiteGeo.description: geo.json — the spatial kernel against turf/geolib/flatbush: the equivalence checks first, then the rows they license.

SuiteJslt.description: jslt.json — the stylesheet engine by scenario, with the compile-mean row and the scenario descriptions the page prints.

SuiteJsonpatch.description: jsonpatch.json — RFC 6902/7396 appliers, their conformance count, and the compile row.

SuiteJsonpath.description: jsonpath.json — the RFC 9535 compliance matrix and the profile: per-selector rows, the compile row, and the scale and early-exit series.

SuiteJsonpointer.description: jsonpointer.json — compiled getters against the interpretive resolver and the npm package, plus the compile row.

SuiteJsonquery.description: jsonquery.json — the query engine by scenario against fontoxpath and JSONata, with the compile-mean row.

SuiteLive.description: live.json — the live-query layer: one meta block naming the runtime, the sizes, the incremental and event-time speedups and the published losses, and the timing tables.

SuiteLongHorizon.description: long-horizon.json — the agent long-horizon suite: the run meta (including what a missing key made it skip), the headline, the tables and one row per configuration.

SuiteMarkdown.description: markdown.json — the Markdown engine against four rivals: the CommonMark and GFM scorecards and the render profile.

SuiteMermaid.description: mermaid.json — the diagram engine against the jison-based reference: the per-diagram scorecard and the parse profile.

SuiteOrm.description: orm.json — the ORM comparison: one meta block of corpus sizes, engines and published losses, and the timing tables (a Bun leg only when Bun ran).

SuiteRetrieval.description: retrieval.json — the retrieval instrument: the run meta (the corpus seed and sizes, the question counts, the reference embedder behind the ranked row, the live tier's status and the synthetic-corpus note), the headline, one table per corpus size and one row per policy per size.

ranked.description: The identity of the deterministic reference embedder behind the near row — a mechanism score, never a model-quality claim.

live.description: Present only when --live scored a near-live row: the provider, the embedding model, its width and the sizes it ran at. The tracked file never carries it.

SuiteSeries.description: series.json — the temporal ground, measured before a kernel exists: the run meta (the corpus and its law, the rounds per row, the SQLite plans read from the host, the derived ratios and the notes), the equivalence checks that gate every timing, the timing and plan tables, and one flat row per route per leg with the answer size it produced.

origin.description: The instant the corpus starts at, in epoch milliseconds — the origin every bucket boundary is measured from.

law.description: The closed form every sample's value comes from, so a reader can regenerate the corpus rather than trust it.

rounds.description: Measured rounds per row family: the default, the fewer a tens-of-milliseconds query row needs, and the many a microsecond index read needs before the clock can see it.

legs.description: One entry per corpus size measured.

plans.description: What SQLite said it would do, read from EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN on the measuring host rather than asserted — a search against a scan is the whole claim of the declared-column row. The store rows carry the plan MODE the planner chose in front of it, so a refinement that quietly stopped being one is visible here.

figures.description: The ratios the notes and the published prose are derived from, so a verdict can never outlive the number it was drawn from. Every one is taken at the leg `largest` names.

kernelBucketVsOnePass.description: What the kernel's fixed-bucket resample costs against the one-pass loop written for that one question. The loop is the ceiling, not a rival: it validates nothing, normalizes nothing and answers one shape.

kernelBucketVsQuery.description: How much faster the kernel answers than the generic query route a consumer had before it — the gap the temporal kernel exists to close, measured against the ground published before it existed.

providerCost.description: What routing every bucket boundary through an injected zone provider costs against the integer ladder, over an identical answer.

fillCost.description: What the fill pass costs on its own: the same corpus and the same ladder, emitting the empty buckets against omitting them.

kernelAsOfVsStored.description: The resident as-of join against one index read per left row, with a left side of a few dozen rows — the shape the index wins, published as the loss it is.

kernelAsOfDenseVsStored.description: The same pair at one left row per hundred right ones — the shape the sorted walk wins.

renderReduction.description: How many source points each rendered point stands for at the largest leg.

noisiestRoute.description: The route whose own rounds disagreed most at the largest leg — the tolerance every ratio above is read with.

storeRangeVsSql.description: The planned range through the store against the same range as a hand-written statement. The store renders and parses a whole JSON document per row where the statement selects two columns, so this prices storing DOCUMENTS rather than planning them.

storeRangeVsResident.description: The planned range against the resident sorted cut — the durability price, published rather than netted out.

storeBucketVsSql.description: The pushed bucket ladder against the same GROUP BY written by hand.

storeBucketVsQuery.description: How much FASTER the pushed bucket is than the generic query route the vocabulary had before it — the native-against-document figure.

storeBucketVsResident.description: The pushed bucket against the one-pass loop in memory.

storeRollingVsResident.description: A window measured in time is a named refinement, never pushed: the index bounds the fetch and the temporal kernel decides. This is what that costs against the same kernel over an array already in memory.

storeAsOfVsIndexReads.description: The batched as-of join against one index read per left row. Above 1 the batch is SLOWER and the row says so: with no tolerance a backward join can only be bounded above.

storeAsOfCandidates.description: How many rows the batched join actually read — an ACTUAL count taken from the run, never an estimate.

storeAsOfStatements.description: How many statements the batched join issued, whatever the probes numbered. The bound is the claim.

storeRollingCandidates.description: How many rows the rolling refinement handed to the kernel.

spread.description: p75/p25 over that row's own measured rounds — the tolerance it was drawn with, so two runs can be compared against a published number rather than an invented one.

results.description: How many rows that route answered — a timing beside an answer size, so a faster row that answered less is visible as one.

SuiteSpatial.description: spatial.json — spatial storage in @jarenjs/db: one meta block (the corpus, the probe, the corpus gate, the derived figures and the notes that name the rivals), the equivalence checks, and the timing tables — one row per way the same predicate can run.

mappings.description: The physical realizations of derive: 'bbox' the run measured, read AND load.

SuiteToml.description: toml.json — the JOSL reader and writer against the TOML field: the toml-test compliance blocks, the parse/stringify profile and the streaming record.

SuiteValidate.description: validate.json — the JSON Schema run: the run metadata, the per-engine summary, one row per official-suite test and the tests that errored.

SuiteVector.description: vector.json — k-nearest over a derive: 'vector' column, measured every physical way it runs: the run meta (the grid, the probes, the rival and its loadability, the rival-disagreement classes with their pinned sizes, the derived figures and the notes), the equivalence checks that gate every timing, the query and price tables, one flat row per path per leg, and the storage measurements per leg.

legs.description: One entry per corpus size x width measured, with the column the plan read and the candidates its cut kept.

rival.description: The measured rival, or the exact reason it did not load on the measuring host — never silently dropped.

classes.description: How the rival's answers related to this suite's, counted into named classes with pinned sizes: a rival that answers differently is a finding, not a tolerance.

figures.description: The ratios the notes and the published prose are derived from, so a verdict can never outlive the number it was drawn from.

SuiteView.description: view.json — the view engine: the build/update/SSR/frame/memo tables and the corpus the run used.

site.packages.doc: The package census: the published workspaces of this repository, in manifest order, each in its own manifest's words. generated and commit are the HEAD commit's date and hash — null in a checkout without git, which is the honest answer, not a wall clock.

site.content.doc: The site content the workspaces own: one entry per published workspace, in the census's order, carrying the card the package wrote for itself, the engine grid mapping it claims, and its documentation section as a parsed Markdown document. `docs` is declared open here on purpose — its grammar is the Markdown AST @jarenjs/md publishes (components/md/schemas/jaren-md-ast.schema.json), and a copy of that grammar in this document would be a second one to keep true.

site.cards.doc: The cards half of the site content: every entry site.content answers, minus the documentation body. The home page draws its engine grid from a few hundred bytes per workspace, while the markdown sections — which are the bulk of the other artifact — are fetched only by the page that renders them.

reproducible.description: The bundle is tied to a commit AND the tree matched it.

site.build.doc: The build provenance the footer prints: which version, which revision and which toolchain produced the deployed bundle. Deliberately not measurement provenance — the gap between the two is what the site shows.

source.description: The committed fixture this was projected from, repo-relative.

mappings.description: The model each store runner answers under: with the derived spatial indexes over four generated columns, with the same indexes realized as R*Tree virtual tables, and with none at all. The logical model is the same in the first two; only the shape on disk differs, and an answer that differs with it would falsify the separation.

skipped.description: Entries a second executor is not asked to answer, left out by their marker and named so a runner that ran none of them ran none on purpose.

site.corpus.doc: The committed spatial corpus, projected for a store: every entry the JavaScript engine recorded an answer for, as the documents to insert and the query to run over them, under three models — the derived spatial indexes over generated columns, the same indexes as R*Trees, and none. The data studio posts each entry to its worker so that SQLite compiled to wasm — the third executor, beside the engine and the Node driver — is held to the same recorded answers in a real browser tab. Projected from the fixture by the build, never copied by hand.

bench.meta.doc: Everything the overview needs without loading the big suite files: the run stamp, the conformance blocks, the XQuery scorecard and one headline row per published suite with the provenance of the run that measured it. This is the shape the generator writes and the browser reads, and the pair agreeing is what this operation exists to enforce.

bench.suite.doc: One benchmark suite's payload. The twenty-five suites are genuinely heterogeneous — a per-test table, a compliance matrix, a scenario grid — so each has its own shape here and the output is exactly one of them: every published file matches a single member, which is what makes oneOf the honest connective rather than anyOf. Each shape is closed at its root and closed again over every record the page iterates, so a suite whose generator adds, renames or retypes a member settles as a typed refusal instead of a wrong render — and the fix is one edit to this document in the same commit as the generator's. Depth stops where the page stops reading: a table's columns and rows stay open, because their contents are cells, not a declaration. Measured values are declared number, never integer: a rounded timing that lands on a whole value is an accident of the run.

path.description: A repo-relative Markdown path — a workspace README, or a document a rendered README links to. Bounded here so no other origin and no traversal can reach the raw base.

url.description: The raw URL the document was read from — the dialog resolves the document's own relative links against it.

readme.fetch.doc: A repository Markdown document as raw text, addressed from the one raw base the site keeps. The reader is handed the URL beside the text because the link rewriter resolves against it.
